title: Citizen Weather Observation Weekly Wind Speed Trend
dataSources: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel:reading`), magnetometer (`magnetometer:reading`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`).
app: DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — via MQTT and scripted inputs to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=citizenweather:obs wind_kmh=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(wind_kmh) as avg_duration, max(wind_kmh) as worst_duration by _time
| sort _time
description: Trends the average and worst wind speed for Citizen Weather observation events each week.
value: Weekly timing trends show whether a process is becoming slower, more erratic, or healthier over time.
implementation: Capture wind_kmh on each event and review weekly averages plus worst cases during your personal ops review.
visualization: Line chart of weekly average wind speed with markers for the worst week.
grandmaExplanation: It helps you whether Citizen Weather observation tasks are taking longer than they used to and where the slow weeks were.
